/**

/* doitgen.c: this file is part of PolyBench/C */

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "doitgen.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int nr, int nq, int np,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C4,NP,NP,np,np))
{
  int i, j, k;

  for (i = 0; i < nr; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nq; j++)
      for (k = 0; k < np; k++)
	A[i][j][k] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j + k)%np) / np;
  for (i = 0; i < np; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < np; j++)
      C4[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*j % np) / np;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int nr, int nq, int np,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np))
{
  int i, j, k;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < nr; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nq; j++)
      for (k = 0; k < np; k++) {
	if ((i*nq*np+j*np+k) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j][k]);
      }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
void kernel_doitgen[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int nr, int nq, int np,
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C4,NP,NP,np,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(sum,NP,np))
{
  int r, q, p, s;

#pragma scop
  for (r = 0; r < _PB_NR; r++)
    for (q = 0; q < _PB_NQ; q++)  {
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)  {
	sum[p] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (s = 0; s < _PB_NP; s++)
	  sum[p] += A[r][q][s] * C4[s][p];
      }
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)
	A[r][q][p] = sum[p];
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int nr = NR;
  int nq = NQ;
  int np = NP;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_3D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(sum,DATA_TYPE,NP,np);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C4,DATA_TYPE,NP,NP,np,np);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (nr, nq, np,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C4));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_doitgen (nr, nq, np,
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C4),
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(sum));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(nr, nq, np,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(sum);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C4);

  return 0;
}

domain:
    r: dim in [0, NR)
    q: dim in [0, NQ)
    p: dim in [0, NP)
    s: dim in [0, NP)

data:
    # Logical read-only view of the original content of A.
    # In the C implementation this aliases the same storage as A
    # (no extra full-sized copy is actually allocated).
    A_in[r, q, p]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (r, q, p) -> (r * NQ + q) * NP + p   # row-major over (r,q,p)

    # Output array holding the transformed values; in-place in C.
    A[r, q, p]: out DATA_TYPE
        = (r, q, p) -> (r * NQ + q) * NP + p   # same layout as A_in

    # Constant NP×NP transform matrix.
    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (s, p) -> s * NP + p                 # row-major: s is row, p is column

    # Temporary accumulator vector used to materialize the reduction
    # for a fixed (r, q). Implemented as a private buffer per (r, q)
    # or per thread.
    sum_local[p]: tmp DATA_TYPE
        = p -> p

parameters:
    NR: int          # number of "rows" in the first dimension
    NQ: int          # number of "columns" in the second dimension
    NP: int          # length of the innermost dimension

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen w.r.t. cache & SIMD width).
    TP: int const    # tile size along p (e.g., 32 or 64)
    VF: int const    # SIMD vector width in elements (e.g., 4, 8)
    US: int const    # unroll factor for s (e.g., 4)

computation:
    # High-level semantics:
    # For each (r, q), treat A_in[r, q, *] as a length-NP row vector and
    # right-multiply it by the NP×NP matrix C4. The result overwrites A.
    #
    # The RHS uses the *original* values of A_in[r, q, *]; an implementation
    # may realize this either with a separate output buffer or in-place using
    # a temporary vector (as in the C code).
    for r, q, p:
        A[r, q, p] = sum(s in [0, NP), A_in[r, q, s] * C4[s, p])

dependencies:
    # Each output element A[r, q, p] depends on:
    #   - the entire original row A_in[r, q, 0:NP)
    #   - the entire column C4[0:NP, p]
    # There are no cross-(r, q) dependences, so different (r, q) slices
    # are independent and can be processed in parallel.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP):
        (A_in[r, q, 0:NP], C4[0:NP, p]) -> A[r, q, p]

optimization:
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Realize the reduction with an explicit temporary vector
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Implement the sum() reduction by introducing a 1D accumulator
    # sum_local[p] per (r, q), matching the original 'sum' array.
    # This avoids an O(NP^3) in-place update pattern and allows
    # better reuse of A_in[r, q, s].
    #
    # Pseudo-structure of the realized loops for a fixed (r, q):
    #   for p in [0, NP): sum_local[p] = 0;
    #   for s in [0, NP):
    #       a_rqs = A_in[r, q, s];
    #       for p in [0, NP):
    #           sum_local[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p];
    #   for p in [0, NP): A[r, q, p] = sum_local[p];
    #
    # We express this realization via directives:

    # Make sum_local private to each (r, q) instance / each worker.
    # This ensures race-free parallel execution over r, q.
    # (New directive)
    privatize(sum_local)
    # hoist(r) and hoist(q) conceptually lift the allocation / reuse
    # of sum_local to the outer (r, q) loops.
    hoist(r)
    hoist(q)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Improve arithmetic intensity and locality inside (r, q)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The inner reduction is originally expressed as a sum over s.
    # Realize it with the loop order (s outer, p inner) so that
    #   - A_in[r, q, s] is loaded once per s and reused across all p.
    #   - C4[s, p] is accessed with p as the innermost index, i.e.,
    #     as a contiguous row of C4 in row-major layout.
    #
    # This is equivalent to an interchange of the conceptual loops
    # over p and s relative to the naive realization.

    interchange(p, s)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Tiling and SIMD along the p-dimension
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block the innermost p loop into tiles of size TP for:
    #   - better cache behavior for sum_local and C4 rows
    #   - straightforward SIMD vectorization along p.
    block(p, P, TP)          # p = P * TP + (inner index over tile)
    hoist(P)                 # move the tile loop outside the innermost loops

    # Within each p-tile, vectorize across the p elements. This maps naturally
    # to contiguous loads/stores of sum_local and C4[s, *].
    vectorize(P, VF)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. Unrolling for instruction-level parallelism
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Unroll the s loop by a small factor to overlap independent multiply-adds,
    # improving ILP without significantly increasing register pressure.
    unroll(s, US)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Parallelism across (r, q)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Different (r, q) slices are independent, so distribute them across cores.
    # Implementation hint: map to OpenMP 'parallel for collapse(2)'.
    parallelize(r)
    parallelize(q)

    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # 6. Data layout choices (kept, but made explicit)
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Keep row-major layouts; with the chosen loop order (s outer, p inner),
    # both A_in[r, q, *] and C4[s, *] are traversed contiguously.
    #
    # Explicitly state layouts to make this contract clear:
    A_in.layout  = (r, q, p) -> (r * NQ + q) * NP + p
    A.layout     = (r, q, p) -> (r * NQ + q) * NP + p
    C4.layout    = (s, p)    -> s * NP + p

    # (Optional but recommended) Ensure A and C4 are aligned to cache-line
    # and SIMD boundaries; this is an implementation detail, not a semantic
    # change, so it is left as a comment rather than a formal directive.
--- END OF MODEL: doitgen-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: doitgen-02 ---
domain:
    r: dim in [0, NR)
    q: dim in [0, NQ)
    p: dim in [0, NP)
    s: dim in [0, NP)

data:
    # 3D array A is laid out as A[nr][nq][np] in C, i.e. p is the
    # fastest-varying index (row-major over the last dimension).
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        (r, q, p) -> ((r * NQ) + q) * NP + p

    # 2D array C4 is C4[np][np], row-major.
    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE =
        (s, p) -> s * NP + p

    # 1D temporary accumulator, reused for each (r, q).
    sum[p]: temp DATA_TYPE =
        p -> p

parameters:
    # Tunable parameters (chosen empirically for the target machine).
    VP: int      # vector width for p-dimension (e.g., 8 for AVX2 double)
    US: int      # unroll factor for s-dimension in the inner kernel

computation:
    # Logical semantics:
    # For each (r, q), the row-vector A[r, q, *] is right-multiplied by
    # the matrix C4, with the result written back to A:
    #
    #   A[r, q, p] := sum_{s=0..NP-1} A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # This matches the effect of the original kernel where, for each
    # fixed (r, q), 'sum[p]' accumulates Σ_s A[r,q,s] * C4[s,p] and is
    # then copied into A[r,q,p].
    for r, q, p:
        A[r, q, p] = sum(s, A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p])

optimization:
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelization
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (r, q) slice A[r, q, *] is independent, so we can execute
    # different r-iterations in parallel.
    parallelize(r)

    # 'sum[p]' must be private to each parallel instance of r (and q)
    # to avoid data races when r is parallelized.
    #
    # privatize(X, {D1, D2, ...}) means:
    #   Logically give X extra indices over D1, D2, ... so that each
    #   dynamic instance of those dimensions uses its own copy of X.
    #   Implementation-wise this is realized with thread-local or
    #   per-iteration storage and does not change sequential semantics.
    privatize(sum, {r, q})

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Locality and arithmetic optimization inside the reduction
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The naive loop structure for the reduction implied by the
    # high-level formula is (per fixed r, q):
    #
    #   for p:
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #       for s:
    #           sum[p] += A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # This keeps s innermost, which walks C4[s, p] with a large stride
    # in memory (fixed p, varying s). We transform it to:
    #
    #   for p:
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #   for s:
    #       a = A[r, q, s]
    #       for p:
    #           sum[p] += a * C4[s, p]
    #
    # so that:
    #   - A[r, q, s] is loaded once per s and reused across all p.
    #   - C4[s, p] and sum[p] are accessed contiguously in p.
    #
    # This is expressed as a loop interchange between p and s in the
    # reduction nest, preserving the per-(r,q,p) accumulation order.
    interchange(p, s)

    # After applying 'interchange(p, s)', an explicit implementation
    # of the semantic assignment becomes (per (r, q)):
    #
    #   for p in [0, NP):                # initialization
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #   for s in [0, NP):                # reduction
    #       a_rqs = A[r, q, s]
    #       for p in [0, NP):
    #           sum[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #   for p in [0, NP):                # write-back
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # using sum[p] as the temporary buffer to implement the
    # mathematically out-of-place transform in-place.

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The innermost p loop now walks contiguous elements of both
    # C4[s, p] and sum[p], which is ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(p, VP)

    # Unroll the s loop to increase ILP and hide FMA/latency, while
    # still streaming over A[r, q, s] and C4[s, p] in cache.
    unroll(s, US)
--- END OF MODEL: doitgen-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: doitgen-03 ---
domain:
    # Problem dimensions
    r: dim in [0, NR)          # first spatial dimension
    q: dim in [0, NQ)          # second spatial dimension
    p: dim in [0, NP)          # contracted/output dimension
    s: dim in [0, NP)          # contracted/input dimension (same extent as p)

data:
    # 3D tensor A, updated in-place
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        (r, q, p) -> ((r * NQ + q) * NP + p)   # row-major, p is fastest-varying

    # 2D transformation matrix C4
    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE =
        (s, p) -> (s * NP + p)                 # row-major, p is fastest-varying

    # 1D temporary buffer "sum" of length NP, reused for each (r, q)
    # In the original C code this is a single global array; for parallel versions
    # it is conceptually privatized per (r, q) / per thread.
    sum[p]: temp DATA_TYPE =
        (p) -> p

parameters:
    # Problem sizes
    NR: index_type
    NQ: index_type
    NP: index_type

    # Tunable blocking parameters (chosen based on cache hierarchy)
    TR: index_type  # tile size along r,   e.g., 4 or 8
    TQ: index_type  # tile size along q,   e.g., 4 or 8
    TS: index_type  # tile size along s,   e.g., 32
    TP: index_type  # tile size along p,   e.g., 64

    # Vectorization parameter
    VEC: index_type # SIMD width for p, e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles, 16 for AVX-512 floats

computation:
    # For each (r, q) slice, we apply the same NP×NP linear transform C4
    # along the last dimension of A:
    #
    #   A[r, q, p] <- sum_{s=0..NP-1} A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # The computation is explicitly scheduled to:
    #   (1) initialize all sum[p],
    #   (2) accumulate over s with p as the innermost loop,
    #   (3) write back to A.
    #
    # This is algebraically equivalent to the original code but:
    #   - each A[r, q, s] is loaded only once per (r, q),
    #   - C4 is traversed row-wise (contiguously) instead of column-wise,
    #   - the innermost loop over p is well-suited for SIMD.

    for r, q:
        INIT_SUM:
            for p:
                sum[p] = 0

        ACCUM:
            # s must be sequential because sum[p] carries a dependence across s
            for s in seq(0, NP):
                a_val = A[r, q, s]          # load once and reuse across all p
                for p:
                    sum[p] += a_val * C4[s, p]

        WRITE_BACK:
            for p:
                A[r, q, p] = sum[p]

dependencies:
    # Intra-(r, q) dependencies:
    #
    # 1. sum[p] must be initialized before it is used in ACCUM at s = 0.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP):
        INIT_SUM(r, q, p) -> ACCUM(r, q, p, s = 0)

    # 2. For fixed (r, q, p), ACCUM at s depends on ACCUM at s-1
    #    because sum[p] is updated cumulatively across s.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP), s in [1, NP):
        ACCUM(r, q, p, s - 1) -> ACCUM(r, q, p, s)

    # 3. WRITE_BACK uses the final sum[p] after all s iterations complete.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP):
        ACCUM(r, q, p, s = NP - 1) -> WRITE_BACK(r, q, p)

    # There are no cross-(r, q) dependencies:
    # for (r1, q1) != (r2, q2) the computations are independent and can be
    # executed in any order or in parallel.

optimization:
    # High-level transformation relative to the original C loops
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Original (within fixed r, q):
    #   for p:
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #       for s:
    #           sum[p] += A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #   for p:
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # Optimized schedule (explicitly encoded in 'computation'):
    #   for p: sum[p] = 0
    #   for s:
    #       tmp = A[r, q, s]
    #       for p: sum[p] += tmp * C4[s, p]
    #   for p: A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # This is a loop interchange of (p, s) plus hoisting of the sum initialization.
    # Benefits:
    #   - Each A[r, q, s] is loaded once instead of NP times.
    #   - C4 is accessed row-contiguously along p, improving cache and SIMD use.
    #   - The innermost loop over p is amenable to vectorization.

    interchange(p, s)   # make p the innermost loop in ACCUM, s outside
    hoist(p)            # hoist sum initialization (and write-back) outside the s loop per (r, q)

    # Parallelization
    # ---------------
    # Exploit outer parallelism over (r, q) slices. Each (r, q) is independent.
    # To avoid races on 'sum', it is privatized per parallel context.
    block(r, Rb, TR)         # tile r into blocks of size TR
    block(q, Qb, TQ)         # tile q into blocks of size TQ
    parallelize(Rb)          # distribute tiles of r (and nested q-tiles) across threads
    # Optionally, an implementation may also distribute over Qb if needed.

    # Custom directive:
    #   privatize(DATA, DIMS) means: give each parallel instance over DIMS its
    #   own logical copy of DATA. Here, implementations typically allocate one
    #   NP-element 'sum' per thread on the stack or in thread-local storage.
    privatize(sum, {r, q})

    # Cache and register blocking for the contraction
    # -----------------------------------------------
    # Block the inner dimensions so that:
    #   - TS controls how many A[r, q, s] elements are processed before reuse,
    #   - TP controls the number of sum[p] and C4[s, p] elements held in
    #     registers / L1 cache at once.
    # Only the logical schedule is expressed here; sum's physical size remains NP.
    block(s, Sb, TS)         # s = Sb * TS + s_local
    block(p, Pb, TP)         # p = Pb * TP + p_local

    # Vectorization and unrolling
    # ---------------------------
    # Vectorize operations along p, where memory is contiguous for both sum and C4.
    vectorize(p, VEC)        # SIMD along p inside the innermost loops
    unroll(s, 4)             # moderate unrolling of s to increase ILP

    # Notes:
    # - The chosen TR, TQ, TS, TP, and VEC should be tuned for the target CPU
    #   (e.g., L1/L2 sizes and SIMD width).
    # - The overall memory footprint remains essentially unchanged:
    #     * A and C4 are unchanged.
    #     * sum remains size NP, replicated only per thread via 'privatize',
    #       which is far below the +50% memory budget even with many threads.
--- END OF MODEL: doitgen-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: doitgen-04 ---
domain:
    r: dim in [0, NR)
    q: dim in [0, NQ)
    p: dim in [0, NP)
    s: dim in [0, NP)

data:
    # 3D array A: A[r][q][p] in C code, row-major with p as fastest index
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        (r, q, p) -> (r * NQ + q) * NP + p  # Row-major

    # 2D transform matrix C4: C4[s][p] in C code, row-major
    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE =
        (s, p) -> s * NP + p                # Row-major, p-contiguous per fixed s

    # Per-(r,q) scratch vector used to hold the reduction result.
    # In the original C code this is a single NP-length array "sum" reused
    # across all (r,q). Here we model it conceptually as a local buffer
    # to enable parallel (r,q) execution; implementation uses one scratch
    # vector per thread.
    sum_local[p]: temp DATA_TYPE           # Size NP, kept in fast memory

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (compile-time or run-time)
    NR: int
    NQ: int
    NP: int

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    RB: int  # tile size along r (outermost)
    QB: int  # tile size along q
    SB: int  # tile size along s (reduction dimension)
    PB: int  # tile size along p (output dimension)
    VEC: int # vector width for p-dimension SIMD (e.g., 4, 8, 16)
    UP: int  # unroll factor for inner p-loop
    US: int  # unroll factor for inner s-loop

computation:
    # Logical specification:
    # For each (r, q), the NP-length row A[r, q, *] is multiplied on the right
    # by the common NP×NP matrix C4. That is, for every output index p:
    #
    #   A_new[r, q, p] = sum_{s=0}^{NP-1} A_old[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # The implementation uses a temporary vector (sum_local) to avoid
    # overwriting A while it is still needed on the right-hand side.
    for r, q, p:
        A[r, q, p] = sum(s in [0, NP), A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p])

dependencies:
    # For each fixed (r, q), all outputs A[r, q, p] depend on the entire
    # original row A[r, q, *]. This creates a true flow dependence along p:
    #
    #   A[r, q, s] (old) -> A[r, q, p] (new)  for all p, s in [0, NP)
    #
    # Hence, a naive in-place update without a temporary would be incorrect.
    # A correct schedule must read all A[r, q, s] values from the pre-update
    # state and only then overwrite A[r, q, *].
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP), s in [0, NP):
        A[r, q, s] (read) -> A[r, q, p] (write)

optimization:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Parallelize across independent (r, q) planes with outer tiling.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (r, q) pair is completely independent given read-only C4.
    # We therefore tile the (r, q) space and parallelize over r-tiles.
    block(r, R, RB)        # R: tile index along r, tile size RB
    block(q, Q, QB)        # Q: tile index along q, tile size QB
    hoist(R)               # Make R the outermost loop
    hoist(Q)               # Next outermost: process 2D tiles in (r, q)

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "doitgen.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int nr, int nq, int np,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C4,NP,NP,np,np))
{
  int i, j, k;

  for (i = 0; i < nr; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nq; j++)
      for (k = 0; k < np; k++)
	A[i][j][k] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j + k)%np) / np;
  for (i = 0; i < np; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < np; j++)
      C4[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*j % np) / np;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int nr, int nq, int np,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np))
{
  int i, j, k;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < nr; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nq; j++)
      for (k = 0; k < np; k++) {
	if ((i*nq*np+j*np+k) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j][k]);
      }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
void kernel_doitgen[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int nr, int nq, int np,
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C4,NP,NP,np,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(sum,NP,np))
{
  int r, q, p, s;

#pragma scop
  for (r = 0; r < _PB_NR; r++)
    for (q = 0; q < _PB_NQ; q++)  {
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)  {
	sum[p] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (s = 0; s < _PB_NP; s++)
	  sum[p] += A[r][q][s] * C4[s][p];
      }
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)
	A[r][q][p] = sum[p];
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int nr = NR;
  int nq = NQ;
  int np = NP;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_3D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(sum,DATA_TYPE,NP,np);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C4,DATA_TYPE,NP,NP,np,np);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (nr, nq, np,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C4));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_doitgen (nr, nq, np,
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C4),
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(sum));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(nr, nq, np,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(sum);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C4);

  return 0;
}

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Locality and arithmetic optimization inside the reduction
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The naive loop structure for the reduction implied by the
    # high-level formula is (per fixed r, q):
    #
    #   for p:
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #       for s:
    #           sum[p] += A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # This keeps s innermost, which walks C4[s, p] with a large stride
    # in memory (fixed p, varying s). We transform it to:
    #
    #   for p:
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #   for s:
    #       a = A[r, q, s]
    #       for p:
    #           sum[p] += a * C4[s, p]
    #
    # so that:
    #   - A[r, q, s] is loaded once per s and reused across all p.
    #   - C4[s, p] and sum[p] are accessed contiguously in p.
    #
    # This is expressed as a loop interchange between p and s in the
    # reduction nest, preserving the per-(r,q,p) accumulation order.
    interchange(p, s)

    # of the semantic assignment becomes (per (r, q)):
    #
    #   for p in [0, NP):                # initialization
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #   for s in [0, NP):                # reduction
    #       a_rqs = A[r, q, s]
    #       for p in [0, NP):
    #           sum[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #   for p in [0, NP):                # write-back
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # using sum[p] as the temporary buffer to implement the
    # mathematically out-of-place transform in-place.

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The innermost p loop now walks contiguous elements of both
    # C4[s, p] and sum[p], which is ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(p, VP)

    # Unroll the s loop to increase ILP and hide FMA/latency, while
    # still streaming over A[r, q, s] and C4[s, p] in cache.
    unroll(s, US)

domain:

    q: dim in [0, NQ)          # second spatial dimension
    p: dim in [0, NP)          # contracted/output dimension
    s: dim in [0, NP)          # contracted/input dimension (same extent as p)

data:
    # 3D tensor A, updated in-place
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE =

    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE =

    # In the original C code this is a single global array; for parallel versions
    # it is conceptually privatized per (r, q) / per thread.
    sum[p]: temp DATA_TYPE =
        (p) -> p

parameters:
    # Problem sizes
    NR: index_type
    NQ: index_type
    NP: index_type

    # Tunable blocking parameters (chosen based on cache hierarchy)
    TR: index_type  # tile size along r,   e.g., 4 or 8
    TQ: index_type  # tile size along q,   e.g., 4 or 8
    TS: index_type  # tile size along s,   e.g., 32
    TP: index_type  # tile size along p,   e.g., 64

    VEC: index_type # SIMD width for p, e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles, 16 for AVX-512 floats

    # For each (r, q) slice, we apply the same NP×NP linear transform C4
    # along the last dimension of A:
    #
    #   A[r, q, p] <- sum_{s=0..NP-1} A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # The computation is explicitly scheduled to:
    #   (1) initialize all sum[p],
    #   (2) accumulate over s with p as the innermost loop,
    #   (3) write back to A.
    #
    # This is algebraically equivalent to the original code but:
    #   - each A[r, q, s] is loaded only once per (r, q),
    #   - C4 is traversed row-wise (contiguously) instead of column-wise,
    #   - the innermost loop over p is well-suited for SIMD.

    for r, q:
        INIT_SUM:
            for p:
                sum[p] = 0

        ACCUM:
            # s must be sequential because sum[p] carries a dependence across s
            for s in seq(0, NP):
                a_val = A[r, q, s]          # load once and reuse across all p
                for p:
                    sum[p] += a_val * C4[s, p]

        WRITE_BACK:
            for p:
                A[r, q, p] = sum[p]

dependencies:
    # Intra-(r, q) dependencies:
    #
    # 1. sum[p] must be initialized before it is used in ACCUM at s = 0.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP):
        INIT_SUM(r, q, p) -> ACCUM(r, q, p, s = 0)

    # 2. For fixed (r, q, p), ACCUM at s depends on ACCUM at s-1
    #    because sum[p] is updated cumulatively across s.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP), s in [1, NP):
        ACCUM(r, q, p, s - 1) -> ACCUM(r, q, p, s)

    # 3. WRITE_BACK uses the final sum[p] after all s iterations complete.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP):
        ACCUM(r, q, p, s = NP - 1) -> WRITE_BACK(r, q, p)

    # There are no cross-(r, q) dependencies:
    # for (r1, q1) != (r2, q2) the computations are independent and can be
    # executed in any order or in parallel.

optimization:
    # High-level transformation relative to the original C loops
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Original (within fixed r, q):
    #   for p:
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #       for s:
    #           sum[p] += A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #   for p:
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # Optimized schedule (explicitly encoded in 'computation'):
    #   for p: sum[p] = 0
    #   for s:
    #       tmp = A[r, q, s]
    #       for p: sum[p] += tmp * C4[s, p]
    #   for p: A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # This is a loop interchange of (p, s) plus hoisting of the sum initialization.
    # Benefits:
    #   - Each A[r, q, s] is loaded once instead of NP times.
    #   - C4 is accessed row-contiguously along p, improving cache and SIMD use.
    #   - The innermost loop over p is amenable to vectorization.

    interchange(p, s)   # make p the innermost loop in ACCUM, s outside
    hoist(p)            # hoist sum initialization (and write-back) outside the s loop per (r, q)

    # Parallelization
    # ---------------
    # Exploit outer parallelism over (r, q) slices. Each (r, q) is independent.
    # To avoid races on 'sum', it is privatized per parallel context.
    block(r, Rb, TR)         # tile r into blocks of size TR
    block(q, Qb, TQ)         # tile q into blocks of size TQ
    parallelize(Rb)          # distribute tiles of r (and nested q-tiles) across threads
    # Optionally, an implementation may also distribute over Qb if needed.

    # Custom directive:
    #   privatize(DATA, DIMS) means: give each parallel instance over DIMS its
    #   own logical copy of DATA. Here, implementations typically allocate one
    #   NP-element 'sum' per thread on the stack or in thread-local storage.
    privatize(sum, {r, q})

    # Cache and register blocking for the contraction
    # -----------------------------------------------
    # Block the inner dimensions so that:
    #   - TS controls how many A[r, q, s] elements are processed before reuse,
    #   - TP controls the number of sum[p] and C4[s, p] elements held in
    #     registers / L1 cache at once.
    # Only the logical schedule is expressed here; sum's physical size remains NP.
    block(s, Sb, TS)         # s = Sb * TS + s_local
    block(p, Pb, TP)         # p = Pb * TP + p_local

    # Vectorization and unrolling
    # ---------------------------
    # Vectorize operations along p, where memory is contiguous for both sum and C4.
    vectorize(p, VEC)        # SIMD along p inside the innermost loops
    unroll(s, 4)             # moderate unrolling of s to increase ILP

    # Notes:
    # - The chosen TR, TQ, TS, TP, and VEC should be tuned for the target CPU
    #   (e.g., L1/L2 sizes and SIMD width).
    # - The overall memory footprint remains essentially unchanged:
    #     * A and C4 are unchanged.
    #     * sum remains size NP, replicated only per thread via 'privatize',
    #       which is far below the +50% memory budget even with many threads.

domain:
    r: dim in [0, NR)
    q: dim in [0, NQ)
    p: dim in [0, NP)
    s: dim in [0, NP)

data:
    # 3D array A: A[r][q][p] in C code, row-major with p as fastest index
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        (r, q, p) -> (r * NQ + q) * NP + p  # Row-major

    # 2D transform matrix C4: C4[s][p] in C code, row-major
    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE =
        (s, p) -> s * NP + p                # Row-major, p-contiguous per fixed s

    # Per-(r,q) scratch vector used to hold the reduction result.
    # In the original C code this is a single NP-length array "sum" reused
    # across all (r,q). Here we model it conceptually as a local buffer
    # to enable parallel (r,q) execution; implementation uses one scratch
    # vector per thread.
    sum_local[p]: temp DATA_TYPE           # Size NP, kept in fast memory

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (compile-time or run-time)
    NR: int
    NQ: int
    NP: int

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    RB: int  # tile size along r (outermost)
    QB: int  # tile size along q
    SB: int  # tile size along s (reduction dimension)
    PB: int  # tile size along p (output dimension)
    VEC: int # vector width for p-dimension SIMD (e.g., 4, 8, 16)
    UP: int  # unroll factor for inner p-loop
    US: int  # unroll factor for inner s-loop

computation:
    # Logical specification:
    # For each (r, q), the NP-length row A[r, q, *] is multiplied on the right
    # by the common NP×NP matrix C4. That is, for every output index p:
    #
    #   A_new[r, q, p] = sum_{s=0}^{NP-1} A_old[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # The implementation uses a temporary vector (sum_local) to avoid
    # overwriting A while it is still needed on the right-hand side.
    for r, q, p:
        A[r, q, p] = sum(s in [0, NP), A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p])

dependencies:
    # For each fixed (r, q), all outputs A[r, q, p] depend on the entire
    # original row A[r, q, *]. This creates a true flow dependence along p:
    #
    #   A[r, q, s] (old) -> A[r, q, p] (new)  for all p, s in [0, NP)
    #
    # Hence, a naive in-place update without a temporary would be incorrect.
    # A correct schedule must read all A[r, q, s] values from the pre-update
    # state and only then overwrite A[r, q, *].
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP), s in [0, NP):
        A[r, q, s] (read) -> A[r, q, p] (write)

optimization:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Parallelize across independent (r, q) planes with outer tiling.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (r, q) pair is completely independent given read-only C4.
    # We therefore tile the (r, q) space and parallelize over r-tiles.
    block(r, R, RB)        # R: tile index along r, tile size RB
    block(q, Q, QB)        # Q: tile index along q, tile size QB
    hoist(R)               # Make R the outermost loop
    hoist(Q)               # Next outermost: process 2D tiles in (r, q)
    parallelize(R)         # Distribute r-tiles across threads

    # Implementation note: sum_local[p] is privatized per thread (or per
    # parallel (r, q) instance), so threads do not race on this buffer.
    # Memory overhead: O(#threads * NP * sizeof(DATA_TYPE)), which is
    # negligible compared to |A| and well below the 50% growth budget.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Exploit structure of the reduction for locality and reuse.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Starting from the mathematical reduction
    #   A[r, q, p] = sum_s A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    # we implement, for each fixed (r, q), the following GEMV-like kernel:
    #
    #   for p in [0, NP):               # initialize reduction buffer
    #       sum_local[p] = 0
    #   for s in [0, NP):               # reduction over s
    #       a_rqs = A[r, q, s]          # load once
    #       for p in [0, NP):           # accumulate along p
    #           sum_local[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #   for p in [0, NP):               # write back
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum_local[p]
    #
    # Compared to the original C code (which loops p outer, then s),
    # this schedule:
    #   - Reads each A[r, q, s] exactly once and reuses it across all p.
    #   - Accesses C4[s, p] with p as the innermost index, which is
    #     contiguous in memory (row-major).
    #   - Performs the same floating-point work but reduces A-traffic
    #     and improves cache/TLB locality.
    #
    # This kernel is obtained by interchanging the order of (p, s)
    # in the reduction and hoisting the initialization of sum_local[p].
    interchange(p, s)      # in the reduction loop defining A[r, q, p]
    hoist(s)               # make s the outer loop inside each (r, q)

    # Optional local algebraic optimization:
    #   For each (r, q), rewrite the reduction as
    #     sum_local[p] = A[r, q, 0] * C4[0, p]
    #     for s in [1, NP): sum_local[p] += A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #   eliminating the explicit zero-initialization loop and one
    #   NP-length addition with zero. This preserves semantics and
    #   slightly reduces the number of adds and stores; modern compilers
    #   may perform this automatically.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Block the (s, p) space for cache reuse on C4 and sum_local.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # C4 and sum_local are both NP-length along p; blocking improves
    # L1/L2 locality when NP is large and enables tuned micro-kernels.
    block(s, S, SB)        # S: tile index along s, tile size SB
    block(p, P, PB)        # P: tile index along p, tile size PB
    hoist(S)               # iterate S outermost inside each (r, q)
    # Resulting inner structure (within a tile of (r, q)):
    #   for S:
    #       for P:
    #           for s in tile S:
    #               a_rqs = A[r, q, s]
    #               for p in tile P:
    #                   sum_local[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD vectorization and unrolling over the innermost p-dimension.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The p-dimension is contiguous for both C4[s, p] and sum_local[p],
    # making it ideal for SIMD. We vectorize and unroll the innermost
    # loop over P (p within a tile).
    vectorize(P, VEC)      # generate SIMD over contiguous p
    unroll(P, UP)          # unroll inner p-loop for better ILP
    unroll(S, US)          # mild unrolling over s to hide FMA latency

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Memory-placement considerations.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # - Keep sum_local in stack or thread-local storage to ensure it
    #   resides in L1/L2 cache and avoid false sharing.
    # - C4 is read-only; allow the compiler to place it in read-only
    #   segments and assume no aliasing with A.
    # - With the above blocking, the working set for each (r, q) tile
    #   (a slice of A plus the full C4 and sum_local) fits comfortably
    #   in the higher-cache levels on the target x64 system.

domain:
    r: dim in [0, NR)          # row index in first dimension of A
    q: dim in [0, NQ)          # row index in second dimension of A
    p: dim in [0, NP)          # output element index within A[r, q, :]
    s: dim in [0, NP)          # reduction index over input A[r, q, :]

data:
    # 3D tensor A, updated in-place.
    # Layout matches C's row-major: A[r][q][p] with p contiguous, then q, then r.
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE
        = (r, q, p) -> ((r * NQ + q) * NP + p)

    # 2D matrix C4, read-only in the kernel.
    # Standard row-major: C4[s][p] with p contiguous.
    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (s, p) -> (s * NP + p)

    # The explicit 1D workspace `sum[p]` from the original C code is modeled
    # as a *local, per-(r,q) temporary vector* implementing the reduction;
    # it does not appear as a global data object here.
    # Implementation detail:
    #   for each (r, q), we allocate a local vector sum[0..NP-1].

parameters:
    # Problem sizes NR, NQ, NP are implicit in the domain bounds.

    # Tuning parameters for optimization (compile-time or launch-time constants).
    TR: int  # tile size for r, e.g., 8–32 depending on cache and NR
    TQ: int  # tile size for q, e.g., 8–32 depending on cache and NQ

    VEC_P: int  # SIMD width in elements along p (e.g., 4 or 8 for double, 8 or 16 for float)
    U_P:   int  # unroll factor for the innermost p loop inside each SIMD chunk
    U_S:   int  # unroll factor for the s loop (small, e.g., 2–4)

computation:
    # High-level mathematical semantics of `kernel_doitgen`:
    # For each (r, q, p), form a linear combination of the row A[r, q, :]
    # with the corresponding column of C4, and overwrite A in place.
    #
    # This matches the original C code:
    #   for (r, q):
    #     for (p): sum[p] = 0;
    #     for (p):
    #       for (s): sum[p] += A[r][q][s] * C4[s][p];
    #     for (p): A[r][q][p] = sum[p];
    #
    # which is equivalent to the reduction below.

    UPDATE_A:
      for r, q, p:
          A[r, q, p] = sum(s, A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p])

    # Notes:
    # - The reduction sum(s, ...) is over s in [0, NP).
    # - All reads of A on the right-hand side conceptually use the "old"
    #   values A_before; the write to A[r, q, p] occurs after the reduction
    #   has completed for that (r, q, p). An implementation uses a local
    #   temporary vector (sum[p]) for each (r, q) to avoid in-place hazards.
    # - Each (r, q) row of A is independent of all others.

dependencies:
    # True data dependencies:
    # - Within a fixed (r, q, p), UPDATE_A(r, q, p) depends on all A[r, q, s]
    #   for s in [0, NP) and on all C4[s, p].
    # - There are no cross-(r, q) dependencies in A or C4.
    #
    # This enables outer parallelism over (r, q) after privatizing the
    # reduction temporary.

    # Using a label for the update:
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP), s in [0, NP):
        A_read(r, q, s) -> UPDATE_A(r, q, p)

optimization:
    #------------------------------
    # 1. Loop reordering for locality and vectorization
    #------------------------------
    # The reduction in `computation` is symmetric in p and s, but the
    # memory layouts favor making p the innermost loop:
    #
    #   - A[r, q, s] is contiguous in s.
    #   - C4[s, p] is contiguous in p for fixed s.
    #
    # Implementation-level order used:
    #   for r, q:
    #     sum[p] = 0           (p innermost, contiguous)
    #     for s:
    #       a_rqs = A[r, q, s]   # scalar load
    #       for p:               # innermost loop
    #         sum[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #     for p:
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # The following interchange expresses this preference.

    interchange(p, s)
        # Interchange the logical roles of p and s in the reduction order
        # so that the innermost loops run along p (contiguous in C4) and
        # the outer reduction loop runs along s.

    #------------------------------
    # 2. Blocking over (r, q) for cache locality and parallel work
    #------------------------------
    # Tile the (r, q) plane. Each tile operates on a small block of
    # rows of A that can stay hot in caches while repeatedly streaming C4.

    block(r, Rb, TR)    # Rb indexes r-tiles of size TR
    block(q, Qb, TQ)    # Qb indexes q-tiles of size TQ
    hoist(Rb)           # Move tile loops to the outermost level
    hoist(Qb)

    # Conceptual loop nest after blocking (ignoring p/s for brevity):
    #
    # for Rb in [0, ceil(NR/TR)):
    #   for Qb in [0, ceil(NQ/TQ)):
    #     for r in tile Rb:
    #       for q in tile Qb:
    #         ... reduction over s and p for this (r, q) ...

    #------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization across tiles (outer parallelism)
    #------------------------------
    # Since different (r, q) rows of A are independent, the outer tile
    # loop over Rb can be parallelized. The reduction temporary sum[p]
    # must be *privatized* per worker (e.g., per OpenMP thread).
    #
    # This does not change asymptotic memory usage: each worker allocates
    # one NP-element buffer for sum[p], and there was already a single
    # NP-element buffer in the sequential baseline.

    parallelize(Rb)
        # Parallelize the Rb loop with:
        # - sum[p] declared private to each worker
        # - A and C4 shared and read-only (except for the final writes to A)

    # Optionally, if NR is small and NQ is large, we could instead
    # parallelize Qb (or both Rb and Qb using a 2D decomposition).

    #------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD vectorization and unrolling on p
    #------------------------------
    # The innermost operations along p are simple FMA-like updates on
    # contiguous memory in sum[p] and C4[s, p]. These are ideal for SIMD.

    vectorize(p, VEC_P)
        # Generate SIMD code for the innermost p loop, with width VEC_P
        # elements (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles, depending on ISA).

    unroll(p, U_P)
        # Unroll the (possibly SIMD) p loop by U_P to expose ILP and
        # reduce loop overhead. U_P is typically small (1–4).

    #------------------------------
    # 5. Unrolling over s and scalar replacement
    #------------------------------
    # Further improve ILP by unrolling the reduction loop over s and
    # keeping A[r, q, s] in a scalar register while iterating over p.

    unroll(s, U_S)
        # Unroll the reduction loop over s by a small factor U_S.

    scalar_replace(A[r, q, s])
        # Non-standard directive:
        #   Load A[r, q, s] into a scalar (e.g., a_rqs) once per (r, q, s)
        #   iteration and reuse it for all p in the innermost loop.
        # This reduces memory traffic by avoiding repeated loads of
        # A[r, q, s] inside the p loop.

    #------------------------------
    # 6. Implementation of the reduction with a local buffer
    #------------------------------
    # To avoid in-place update hazards and preserve the original semantics,
    # the reduction is implemented with a per-(r, q) local buffer sum[p]:
    #
    #   for each tile Rb, Qb (possibly in parallel over Rb):
    #     for each r in tile Rb:
    #       for each q in tile Qb:
    #         # initialize local accumulation vector
    #         for p in [0, NP):
    #             sum[p] = 0
    #         # main reduction, reordered for locality:
    #         for s in [0, NP):
    #             a_rqs = A[r, q, s]
    #             for p in [0, NP):          # vectorized over p
    #                 sum[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #         # write-back
    #         for p in [0, NP):
    #             A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # This algorithm is mathematically equivalent to the high-level
    # reduction in `computation` and respects the original kernel's
    # functionality.

static

		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np))
{

    for (j = 0; j < nq; j++)

void kernel_doitgen[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int nr, int nq, int np,
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C4,NP,NP,np,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(sum,NP,np))
{
  int r, q, p, s;

#pragma scop
  for (r = 0; r < _PB_NR; r++)
    for (q = 0; q < _PB_NQ; q++)  {
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)  {
	sum[p] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (s = 0; s < _PB_NP; s++)
	  sum[p] += A[r][q][s] * C4[s][p];
      }
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)
	A[r][q][p] = sum[p];
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{

  int nr = NR;
  int nq = NQ;

  POLYBENCH_3D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(sum,DATA_TYPE,NP,np);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C4,DATA_TYPE,NP,NP,np,np);

	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),

  polybench_start_instruments;

  kernel_doitgen (nr, nq, np,

		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(sum));

  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(nr, nq, np,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(sum);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C4);

  return 0;
}

    #

    # overwriting A while it is still needed on the right-hand side.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "doitgen.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int nr, int nq, int np,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np),
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C4,NP,NP,np,np))
{
  int i, j, k;

  for (i = 0; i < nr; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nq; j++)
      for (k = 0; k < np; k++)
	A[i][j][k] = (DATA_TYPE) ((i*j + k)%np) / np;
  for (i = 0; i < np; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < np; j++)
      C4[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE) (i*j % np) / np;
}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int nr, int nq, int np,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np))
{
  int i, j, k;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < nr; i++)
    for (j = 0; j < nq; j++)
      for (k = 0; k < np; k++) {
	if ((i*nq*np+j*np+k) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
	fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j][k]);
      }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
void kernel_doitgen[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int nr, int nq, int np,
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C4,NP,NP,np,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(sum,NP,np))
{
  int r, q, p, s;

#pragma scop
  for (r = 0; r < _PB_NR; r++)
    for (q = 0; q < _PB_NQ; q++)  {
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)  {
	sum[p] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (s = 0; s < _PB_NP; s++)
	  sum[p] += A[r][q][s] * C4[s][p];
      }
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)
	A[r][q][p] = sum[p];
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int nr = NR;
  int nq = NQ;
  int np = NP;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_3D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(sum,DATA_TYPE,NP,np);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C4,DATA_TYPE,NP,NP,np,np);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (nr, nq, np,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C4));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_doitgen (nr, nq, np,
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C4),
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(sum));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(nr, nq, np,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(sum);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C4);

  return 0;
}

    # reduction nest, preserving the per-(r,q,p) accumulation order.
    interchange(p, s)

    # of the semantic assignment becomes (per (r, q)):
    #
    #   for p in [0, NP):                # initialization
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #   for s in [0, NP):                # reduction
    #       a_rqs = A[r, q, s]
    #       for p in [0, NP):
    #           sum[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #   for p in [0, NP):                # write-back
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # using sum[p] as the temporary buffer to implement the
    # mathematically out-of-place transform in-place.

    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    #---------------------------------------------------------------
    # The innermost p loop now walks contiguous elements of both
    # C4[s, p] and sum[p], which is ideal for SIMD.
    vectorize(p, VP)

    # still streaming over A[r, q, s] and C4[s, p] in cache.
    unroll(s, US)

domain:

    r: dim in [0, NR)          # first spatial dimension
    q: dim in [0, NQ)          # second spatial dimension
    p: dim in [0, NP)          # contracted/output dimension
    s: dim in [0, NP)          # contracted/input dimension (same extent as p)

data:
    # 3D tensor A, updated in-place
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        (r, q, p) -> ((r * NQ + q) * NP + p)   # row-major, p is fastest-varying

    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE =
        (s, p) -> (s * NP + p)                 # row-major, p is fastest-varying

    # In the original C code this is a single global array; for parallel versions
    # it is conceptually privatized per (r, q) / per thread.
    sum[p]: temp DATA_TYPE =
        (p) -> p

parameters:
    # Problem sizes
    NR: index_type
    NQ: index_type
    NP: index_type

    # Tunable blocking parameters (chosen based on cache hierarchy)
    TR: index_type  # tile size along r,   e.g., 4 or 8
    TQ: index_type  # tile size along q,   e.g., 4 or 8
    TS: index_type  # tile size along s,   e.g., 32
    TP: index_type  # tile size along p,   e.g., 64

    VEC: index_type # SIMD width for p, e.g., 8 for AVX2 doubles, 16 for AVX-512 floats

computation:
    # For each (r, q) slice, we apply the same NP×NP linear transform C4
    # along the last dimension of A:
    #
    #   A[r, q, p] <- sum_{s=0..NP-1} A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # The computation is explicitly scheduled to:
    #   (1) initialize all sum[p],
    #   (2) accumulate over s with p as the innermost loop,
    #   (3) write back to A.
    #
    # This is algebraically equivalent to the original code but:
    #   - each A[r, q, s] is loaded only once per (r, q),
    #   - C4 is traversed row-wise (contiguously) instead of column-wise,
    #   - the innermost loop over p is well-suited for SIMD.

    for r, q:
        INIT_SUM:
            for p:
                sum[p] = 0

        ACCUM:
            # s must be sequential because sum[p] carries a dependence across s
            for s in seq(0, NP):
                a_val = A[r, q, s]          # load once and reuse across all p
                for p:
                    sum[p] += a_val * C4[s, p]

        WRITE_BACK:
            for p:
                A[r, q, p] = sum[p]

dependencies:
    # Intra-(r, q) dependencies:
    #
    # 1. sum[p] must be initialized before it is used in ACCUM at s = 0.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP):
        INIT_SUM(r, q, p) -> ACCUM(r, q, p, s = 0)

    # 2. For fixed (r, q, p), ACCUM at s depends on ACCUM at s-1
    #    because sum[p] is updated cumulatively across s.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP), s in [1, NP):
        ACCUM(r, q, p, s - 1) -> ACCUM(r, q, p, s)

    # 3. WRITE_BACK uses the final sum[p] after all s iterations complete.
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP):
        ACCUM(r, q, p, s = NP - 1) -> WRITE_BACK(r, q, p)

    # There are no cross-(r, q) dependencies:
    # for (r1, q1) != (r2, q2) the computations are independent and can be
    # executed in any order or in parallel.

optimization:
    # High-level transformation relative to the original C loops
    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # Original (within fixed r, q):
    #   for p:
    #       sum[p] = 0
    #       for s:
    #           sum[p] += A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #   for p:
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # Optimized schedule (explicitly encoded in 'computation'):
    #   for p: sum[p] = 0
    #   for s:
    #       tmp = A[r, q, s]
    #       for p: sum[p] += tmp * C4[s, p]
    #   for p: A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # This is a loop interchange of (p, s) plus hoisting of the sum initialization.
    # Benefits:
    #   - Each A[r, q, s] is loaded once instead of NP times.
    #   - C4 is accessed row-contiguously along p, improving cache and SIMD use.
    #   - The innermost loop over p is amenable to vectorization.

    interchange(p, s)   # make p the innermost loop in ACCUM, s outside
    hoist(p)            # hoist sum initialization (and write-back) outside the s loop per (r, q)

    # Parallelization
    # ---------------
    # Exploit outer parallelism over (r, q) slices. Each (r, q) is independent.
    # To avoid races on 'sum', it is privatized per parallel context.
    block(r, Rb, TR)         # tile r into blocks of size TR
    block(q, Qb, TQ)         # tile q into blocks of size TQ
    parallelize(Rb)          # distribute tiles of r (and nested q-tiles) across threads
    # Optionally, an implementation may also distribute over Qb if needed.

    # Custom directive:
    #   privatize(DATA, DIMS) means: give each parallel instance over DIMS its
    #   own logical copy of DATA. Here, implementations typically allocate one
    #   NP-element 'sum' per thread on the stack or in thread-local storage.
    privatize(sum, {r, q})

    # Cache and register blocking for the contraction
    # -----------------------------------------------
    # Block the inner dimensions so that:
    #   - TS controls how many A[r, q, s] elements are processed before reuse,
    #   - TP controls the number of sum[p] and C4[s, p] elements held in
    #     registers / L1 cache at once.
    # Only the logical schedule is expressed here; sum's physical size remains NP.
    block(s, Sb, TS)         # s = Sb * TS + s_local
    block(p, Pb, TP)         # p = Pb * TP + p_local

    # Vectorization and unrolling
    # ---------------------------
    # Vectorize operations along p, where memory is contiguous for both sum and C4.
    vectorize(p, VEC)        # SIMD along p inside the innermost loops
    unroll(s, 4)             # moderate unrolling of s to increase ILP

    # Notes:
    # - The chosen TR, TQ, TS, TP, and VEC should be tuned for the target CPU
    #   (e.g., L1/L2 sizes and SIMD width).
    # - The overall memory footprint remains essentially unchanged:
    #     * A and C4 are unchanged.
    #     * sum remains size NP, replicated only per thread via 'privatize',
    #       which is far below the +50% memory budget even with many threads.

domain:
    r: dim in [0, NR)
    q: dim in [0, NQ)
    p: dim in [0, NP)
    s: dim in [0, NP)

data:
    # 3D array A: A[r][q][p] in C code, row-major with p as fastest index
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE =
        (r, q, p) -> (r * NQ + q) * NP + p  # Row-major

    # 2D transform matrix C4: C4[s][p] in C code, row-major
    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE =
        (s, p) -> s * NP + p                # Row-major, p-contiguous per fixed s

    # Per-(r,q) scratch vector used to hold the reduction result.
    # In the original C code this is a single NP-length array "sum" reused
    # across all (r,q). Here we model it conceptually as a local buffer
    # to enable parallel (r,q) execution; implementation uses one scratch
    # vector per thread.
    sum_local[p]: temp DATA_TYPE           # Size NP, kept in fast memory

parameters:
    # Problem sizes (compile-time or run-time)
    NR: int
    NQ: int
    NP: int

    # Tunable blocking and vectorization parameters
    RB: int  # tile size along r (outermost)
    QB: int  # tile size along q
    SB: int  # tile size along s (reduction dimension)
    PB: int  # tile size along p (output dimension)
    VEC: int # vector width for p-dimension SIMD (e.g., 4, 8, 16)
    UP: int  # unroll factor for inner p-loop
    US: int  # unroll factor for inner s-loop

computation:
    # Logical specification:
    # For each (r, q), the NP-length row A[r, q, *] is multiplied on the right
    # by the common NP×NP matrix C4. That is, for every output index p:
    #
    #   A_new[r, q, p] = sum_{s=0}^{NP-1} A_old[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # The implementation uses a temporary vector (sum_local) to avoid
    # overwriting A while it is still needed on the right-hand side.
    for r, q, p:
        A[r, q, p] = sum(s in [0, NP), A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p])

dependencies:
    # For each fixed (r, q), all outputs A[r, q, p] depend on the entire
    # original row A[r, q, *]. This creates a true flow dependence along p:
    #
    #   A[r, q, s] (old) -> A[r, q, p] (new)  for all p, s in [0, NP)
    #
    # Hence, a naive in-place update without a temporary would be incorrect.
    # A correct schedule must read all A[r, q, s] values from the pre-update
    # state and only then overwrite A[r, q, *].
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP), s in [0, NP):
        A[r, q, s] (read) -> A[r, q, p] (write)

optimization:
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 1. Parallelize across independent (r, q) planes with outer tiling.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Each (r, q) pair is completely independent given read-only C4.
    # We therefore tile the (r, q) space and parallelize over r-tiles.
    block(r, R, RB)        # R: tile index along r, tile size RB
    block(q, Q, QB)        # Q: tile index along q, tile size QB
    hoist(R)               # Make R the outermost loop
    hoist(Q)               # Next outermost: process 2D tiles in (r, q)
    parallelize(R)         # Distribute r-tiles across threads

    # Implementation note: sum_local[p] is privatized per thread (or per
    # parallel (r, q) instance), so threads do not race on this buffer.
    # Memory overhead: O(#threads * NP * sizeof(DATA_TYPE)), which is
    # negligible compared to |A| and well below the 50% growth budget.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 2. Exploit structure of the reduction for locality and reuse.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Starting from the mathematical reduction
    #   A[r, q, p] = sum_s A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    # we implement, for each fixed (r, q), the following GEMV-like kernel:
    #
    #   for p in [0, NP):               # initialize reduction buffer
    #       sum_local[p] = 0
    #   for s in [0, NP):               # reduction over s
    #       a_rqs = A[r, q, s]          # load once
    #       for p in [0, NP):           # accumulate along p
    #           sum_local[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #   for p in [0, NP):               # write back
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum_local[p]
    #
    # Compared to the original C code (which loops p outer, then s),
    # this schedule:
    #   - Reads each A[r, q, s] exactly once and reuses it across all p.
    #   - Accesses C4[s, p] with p as the innermost index, which is
    #     contiguous in memory (row-major).
    #   - Performs the same floating-point work but reduces A-traffic
    #     and improves cache/TLB locality.
    #
    # This kernel is obtained by interchanging the order of (p, s)
    # in the reduction and hoisting the initialization of sum_local[p].
    interchange(p, s)      # in the reduction loop defining A[r, q, p]
    hoist(s)               # make s the outer loop inside each (r, q)

    # Optional local algebraic optimization:
    #   For each (r, q), rewrite the reduction as
    #     sum_local[p] = A[r, q, 0] * C4[0, p]
    #     for s in [1, NP): sum_local[p] += A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #   eliminating the explicit zero-initialization loop and one
    #   NP-length addition with zero. This preserves semantics and
    #   slightly reduces the number of adds and stores; modern compilers
    #   may perform this automatically.

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 3. Block the (s, p) space for cache reuse on C4 and sum_local.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # C4 and sum_local are both NP-length along p; blocking improves
    # L1/L2 locality when NP is large and enables tuned micro-kernels.
    block(s, S, SB)        # S: tile index along s, tile size SB
    block(p, P, PB)        # P: tile index along p, tile size PB
    hoist(S)               # iterate S outermost inside each (r, q)
    # Resulting inner structure (within a tile of (r, q)):
    #   for S:
    #       for P:
    #           for s in tile S:
    #               a_rqs = A[r, q, s]
    #               for p in tile P:
    #                   sum_local[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD vectorization and unrolling over the innermost p-dimension.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The p-dimension is contiguous for both C4[s, p] and sum_local[p],
    # making it ideal for SIMD. We vectorize and unroll the innermost
    # loop over P (p within a tile).
    vectorize(P, VEC)      # generate SIMD over contiguous p
    unroll(P, UP)          # unroll inner p-loop for better ILP
    unroll(S, US)          # mild unrolling over s to hide FMA latency

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # 5. Memory-placement considerations.
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # - Keep sum_local in stack or thread-local storage to ensure it
    #   resides in L1/L2 cache and avoid false sharing.
    # - C4 is read-only; allow the compiler to place it in read-only
    #   segments and assume no aliasing with A.
    # - With the above blocking, the working set for each (r, q) tile
    #   (a slice of A plus the full C4 and sum_local) fits comfortably
    #   in the higher-cache levels on the target x64 system.

domain:
    r: dim in [0, NR)          # row index in first dimension of A
    q: dim in [0, NQ)          # row index in second dimension of A
    p: dim in [0, NP)          # output element index within A[r, q, :]
    s: dim in [0, NP)          # reduction index over input A[r, q, :]

data:
    # 3D tensor A, updated in-place.
    # Layout matches C's row-major: A[r][q][p] with p contiguous, then q, then r.
    A[r, q, p]: inout DATA_TYPE
        = (r, q, p) -> ((r * NQ + q) * NP + p)

    # 2D matrix C4, read-only in the kernel.
    # Standard row-major: C4[s][p] with p contiguous.
    C4[s, p]: in DATA_TYPE
        = (s, p) -> (s * NP + p)

    # The explicit 1D workspace `sum[p]` from the original C code is modeled
    # as a *local, per-(r,q) temporary vector* implementing the reduction;
    # it does not appear as a global data object here.
    # Implementation detail:
    #   for each (r, q), we allocate a local vector sum[0..NP-1].

parameters:
    # Problem sizes NR, NQ, NP are implicit in the domain bounds.

    # Tuning parameters for optimization (compile-time or launch-time constants).
    TR: int  # tile size for r, e.g., 8–32 depending on cache and NR
    TQ: int  # tile size for q, e.g., 8–32 depending on cache and NQ

    VEC_P: int  # SIMD width in elements along p (e.g., 4 or 8 for double, 8 or 16 for float)
    U_P:   int  # unroll factor for the innermost p loop inside each SIMD chunk
    U_S:   int  # unroll factor for the s loop (small, e.g., 2–4)

computation:
    # High-level mathematical semantics of `kernel_doitgen`:
    # For each (r, q, p), form a linear combination of the row A[r, q, :]
    # with the corresponding column of C4, and overwrite A in place.
    #
    # This matches the original C code:
    #   for (r, q):
    #     for (p): sum[p] = 0;
    #     for (p):
    #       for (s): sum[p] += A[r][q][s] * C4[s][p];
    #     for (p): A[r][q][p] = sum[p];
    #
    # which is equivalent to the reduction below.

    UPDATE_A:
      for r, q, p:
          A[r, q, p] = sum(s, A[r, q, s] * C4[s, p])

    # Notes:
    # - The reduction sum(s, ...) is over s in [0, NP).
    # - All reads of A on the right-hand side conceptually use the "old"
    #   values A_before; the write to A[r, q, p] occurs after the reduction
    #   has completed for that (r, q, p). An implementation uses a local
    #   temporary vector (sum[p]) for each (r, q) to avoid in-place hazards.
    # - Each (r, q) row of A is independent of all others.

dependencies:
    # True data dependencies:
    # - Within a fixed (r, q, p), UPDATE_A(r, q, p) depends on all A[r, q, s]
    #   for s in [0, NP) and on all C4[s, p].
    # - There are no cross-(r, q) dependencies in A or C4.
    #
    # This enables outer parallelism over (r, q) after privatizing the
    # reduction temporary.

    # Using a label for the update:
    for r in [0, NR), q in [0, NQ), p in [0, NP), s in [0, NP):
        A_read(r, q, s) -> UPDATE_A(r, q, p)

optimization:
    #------------------------------
    # 1. Loop reordering for locality and vectorization
    #------------------------------
    # The reduction in `computation` is symmetric in p and s, but the
    # memory layouts favor making p the innermost loop:
    #
    #   - A[r, q, s] is contiguous in s.
    #   - C4[s, p] is contiguous in p for fixed s.
    #
    # Implementation-level order used:
    #   for r, q:
    #     sum[p] = 0           (p innermost, contiguous)
    #     for s:
    #       a_rqs = A[r, q, s]   # scalar load
    #       for p:               # innermost loop
    #         sum[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #     for p:
    #       A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # The following interchange expresses this preference.

    interchange(p, s)
        # Interchange the logical roles of p and s in the reduction order
        # so that the innermost loops run along p (contiguous in C4) and
        # the outer reduction loop runs along s.

    #------------------------------
    # 2. Blocking over (r, q) for cache locality and parallel work
    #------------------------------
    # Tile the (r, q) plane. Each tile operates on a small block of
    # rows of A that can stay hot in caches while repeatedly streaming C4.

    block(r, Rb, TR)    # Rb indexes r-tiles of size TR
    block(q, Qb, TQ)    # Qb indexes q-tiles of size TQ
    hoist(Rb)           # Move tile loops to the outermost level
    hoist(Qb)

    # Conceptual loop nest after blocking (ignoring p/s for brevity):
    #
    # for Rb in [0, ceil(NR/TR)):
    #   for Qb in [0, ceil(NQ/TQ)):
    #     for r in tile Rb:
    #       for q in tile Qb:
    #         ... reduction over s and p for this (r, q) ...

    #------------------------------
    # 3. Parallelization across tiles (outer parallelism)
    #------------------------------
    # Since different (r, q) rows of A are independent, the outer tile
    # loop over Rb can be parallelized. The reduction temporary sum[p]
    # must be *privatized* per worker (e.g., per OpenMP thread).
    #
    # This does not change asymptotic memory usage: each worker allocates
    # one NP-element buffer for sum[p], and there was already a single
    # NP-element buffer in the sequential baseline.

    parallelize(Rb)
        # Parallelize the Rb loop with:
        # - sum[p] declared private to each worker
        # - A and C4 shared and read-only (except for the final writes to A)

    # Optionally, if NR is small and NQ is large, we could instead
    # parallelize Qb (or both Rb and Qb using a 2D decomposition).

    #------------------------------
    # 4. SIMD vectorization and unrolling on p
    #------------------------------
    # The innermost operations along p are simple FMA-like updates on
    # contiguous memory in sum[p] and C4[s, p]. These are ideal for SIMD.

    vectorize(p, VEC_P)
        # Generate SIMD code for the innermost p loop, with width VEC_P
        # elements (e.g., 4 or 8 for doubles, depending on ISA).

    unroll(p, U_P)
        # Unroll the (possibly SIMD) p loop by U_P to expose ILP and
        # reduce loop overhead. U_P is typically small (1–4).

    #------------------------------
    # 5. Unrolling over s and scalar replacement
    #------------------------------
    # Further improve ILP by unrolling the reduction loop over s and
    # keeping A[r, q, s] in a scalar register while iterating over p.

    unroll(s, U_S)
        # Unroll the reduction loop over s by a small factor U_S.

    scalar_replace(A[r, q, s])
        # Non-standard directive:
        #   Load A[r, q, s] into a scalar (e.g., a_rqs) once per (r, q, s)
        #   iteration and reuse it for all p in the innermost loop.
        # This reduces memory traffic by avoiding repeated loads of
        # A[r, q, s] inside the p loop.

    #------------------------------
    # 6. Implementation of the reduction with a local buffer
    #------------------------------
    # To avoid in-place update hazards and preserve the original semantics,
    # the reduction is implemented with a per-(r, q) local buffer sum[p]:
    #
    #   for each tile Rb, Qb (possibly in parallel over Rb):
    #     for each r in tile Rb:
    #       for each q in tile Qb:
    #         # initialize local accumulation vector
    #         for p in [0, NP):
    #             sum[p] = 0
    #         # main reduction, reordered for locality:
    #         for s in [0, NP):
    #             a_rqs = A[r, q, s]
    #             for p in [0, NP):          # vectorized over p
    #                 sum[p] += a_rqs * C4[s, p]
    #         # write-back
    #         for p in [0, NP):
    #             A[r, q, p] = sum[p]
    #
    # This algorithm is mathematically equivalent to the high-level
    # reduction in `computation` and respects the original kernel's
    # functionality.

/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
void kernel_doitgen[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int nr, int nq, int np,
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_3D(A,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(C4,NP,NP,np,np),
		    DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_1D(sum,NP,np))
{
  int r, q, p, s;

#pragma scop
  for (r = 0; r < _PB_NR; r++)
    for (q = 0; q < _PB_NQ; q++)  {
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)  {
	sum[p] = SCALAR_VAL(0.0);
	for (s = 0; s < _PB_NP; s++)
	  sum[p] += A[r][q][s] * C4[s][p];
      }
      for (p = 0; p < _PB_NP; p++)
	A[r][q][p] = sum[p];
    }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{

  int nr = NR;
  int nq = NQ;
  int np = NP;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_3D_ARRAY_DECL(A,DATA_TYPE,NR,NQ,NP,nr,nq,np);
  POLYBENCH_1D_ARRAY_DECL(sum,DATA_TYPE,NP,np);
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(C4,DATA_TYPE,NP,NP,np,np);

  init_array (nr, nq, np,
	      POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),

  polybench_start_instruments;

  kernel_doitgen (nr, nq, np,
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A),
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(C4),
		  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(sum));

  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(nr, nq, np,  POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(sum);
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(C4);

  return 0;
}

    # Logical specification:
    # For each (r, q), the NP-length row A[r, q, *] is multiplied on the right
    # by the common NP×NP matrix C4. That is, for every output index p:
    #
    #   A_new[r, q, p] = sum_{s=0}^{NP-1} A_old[r, q, s] * C4[s, p]
    #
    # The implementation uses a temporary vector (sum_local) to avoid
    # overwriting A while it is still needed on the right-hand side.
    for r, q, p:

    #

    #

    # A correct schedule must read all A[r, q, s] values from the pre-update

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------

    # We therefore tile the (r, q) space and parallelize over r-tiles.

    block(q, Q, QB)        # Q: tile index along q, tile size QB

    #

    #   - Accesses C4[s, p] with p as the innermost index, which is
    #     contiguous in memory (row-major).
    #   - Performs the same floating-point work but reduces A-traffic

    #
